newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court rejects British Airways airport plea.
newsitem.headline: French court rejects British Airways airport plea.

text.p: A French court on Wednesday rejected an urgent plea by British Airways Plc that Algeria's national airline be barred from serving passengers at a counter next to BA's at Paris' Charles de Gaulle airport.
An administrative court in Melun, suburban Paris, said there were insufficient grounds to act on an urgent basis but agreed to rule at a later date on the substance of the BA complaint.

BA has refused to use its check-in desks at the Charles de Gaulle airport since Air Algerie became its neighbour last month, because of fears that it would be a target for Islamic guerrillas. It has been processing passengers at another site.
It wants to shift its flights to Orly airport on the other side of Paris unless Air Algerie is itself moved to a more secure area.
U.S. airline Trans World Airlines has also expressed concern about security at the airport.
The Paris airport authority, however, has concluded that security at Charles de Gaulle was adequate, and has also turned down BA's plea that it be allowed to move to Orly.
British Airways had urgently asked the court to bar Air Algerie from oprating from its new counter at Charles de Gaulle airport until "adequate security measures" had been taken.
